tiles: Autonomous agent writes, schedules, and posts across platforms
Engagement monitoring catches replies and opportunities in real time
Scheduling optimizes itself against accumulated performance data
Make.com orchestrates the full loop without daily human input
challenge: Social media is the kind of work that eats an owner alive — daily posting, replies, trend response, and weekly analytics. Businesses either let it slide or outsource it at $3–8k/month to an agency. I wanted to see how much of that job could actually be run by an agent rather than chopped into disconnected AI tools that still need a human driver.
approach: I built an agentic system where a single LLM-driven agent owns the full social workflow. It drafts platform-appropriate posts, schedules them against learned engagement windows, monitors replies and mentions for response opportunities, and re-reads its own analytics each week to adjust strategy. Make.com wires the agent into each platform's API so it can actually publish, listen, and react — not just generate text.
result: The system keeps a consistent, on-brand presence across platforms with no daily human involvement, and engagement has trended up as the scheduling model accumulates data. Output quality is within the range of what a dedicated social manager would produce, at a fraction of the cost. It's the most complete example I have of an agent doing a whole job, not just a task inside one.
